public_projection.name: Push an object to a goal
public_projection.objective: Use end-effector contact to push a tabletop object until its position is within the goal region.
scene_context: A small rigid object and a planar goal marker are placed on the tabletop within the arm workspace.
The object has enough clearance for a planar pushing motion and does not require lifting.

start_position.description: Initial position of the manipulated task entity. It is not an end-effector waypoint; use grasp_position when supplied or derive a task-appropriate grasp waypoint.

contact_position.description: World-frame end-effector contact waypoint. Establish contact here before any route_position or tool_target_position.

target_position.description: Desired terminal position of the affected task entity or fixture. It is an end-effector waypoint only for a direct reach task.

target_angle.description: Desired terminal angle of the affected task fixture. It is not a robot wrist-joint target.

tool_target_position.description: Final world-frame end-effector waypoint that drives the contacted or grasped task entity toward target_position. Visit it after contact or grasp and any route_position.

release_position.description: World-frame end-effector carrying waypoint at the placement region. Maintain grasp while moving here and release only after arrival, except an insertion task may retain grasp.

route_position.description: Intermediate world-frame end-effector waypoint between contact or grasp and tool_target_position. Visit it before tool_target_position.

source_refs.specific_reference: metaworld/envs/sawyer_push_v3.py, line 31 and evaluate_state lines 88-112 at pinned commit: TARGET_RADIUS is 0.05 and success is target_to_obj <= TARGET_RADIUS.
source_refs.adaptation: Keep the source 0.05 m object-to-goal obligation and measure it between SO-101 scene bodies after contact-driven pushing; replace only Sawyer geometry and private object placement.

public_projection.name: Single-step ascent
public_projection.objective: Walk straight over one positive step so both front and hind feet completely traverse it within 10 seconds, in all ten trials.
scene_context: One rigid step spans the confined lane; completion places every foot center at least one foot radius beyond the true edge at x = 0.4 m.

source_refs.specific_reference: Results p. 4: each trial runs straight for 10 s; success requires both front and hind legs to traverse the step; ten trials are run per height.
source_refs.adaptation: The obstacle remains morphology-scaled by 0.54 and the 10 second outcome window is retained. The fixed 0.2 m/s command is removed so ReCAP selects speed from closed-loop observations; this is an outcome-based adapted protocol rather than a strict fixed-speed reproduction.

private_guards.adaptation_note: Private Go2 morphology guard: reject fallen or ground-sliding terminal states; these values are not claimed as source benchmark thresholds.

public_projection.objective: Follow a fixed path over an inclined platform, raised platform, stairs, and a block pile without assistance.
scene_context: The four obstacle families appear once in source order and dimensions are scaled uniformly by 0.54.
Trusted completion gates use the actual far edges at x = 0.962, 1.82, 2.4915, and 4.28 m, followed by the finish at 4.8 m.

source_refs.specific_reference: Results Fig. 4C-D: the fixed path traverses the inclined platform, raised platform, stairs, and block pile smoothly without assistance.
source_refs.adaptation: Obstacle dimensions remain uniformly scaled by 0.54. The corrected audit uses a 25 second execution window and requires trusted foot contact with the inclined platform, raised platform, stairs, and block family.
